nodes.label: Discorsi as Lossy Compression of Livy
nodes.rationale: Treat the Discorsi as lossy compression of Livy and decompress it: recover the implicit data model of political information by aligning chapters with Livian sources and classifying each information unit's fate.
nodes.norm_label: discorsi as lossy compression of livy

nodes.label: Loss Gradient
nodes.rationale: Across 44 unit-level alignments: material resources 100% omitted or abstracted, named actors 75%, administrative actions 71%, while historical events (22%) and causal structure (31%) survive. Machiavelli adds model and deletes measurement.

nodes.label: Florentine Fingerprint
nodes.rationale: Where Machiavelli's mechanisms need datasets Rome could not have produced (benefaction recipient rolls, patronage ledgers), Renaissance Florence did produce them; his private-favors typology is a Florentine record-producing inventory wearing a toga.

nodes.label: Dataset Levels A/B/C
nodes.rationale: Grading for dataset hypotheses: A = attested in ancient sources, B = structure implied but values lost, C = hypothetical; never fabricated.

nodes.label: Evidence Classes (Five Strata)
nodes.rationale: Every statement belongs to exactly one of five strata with explicit evidence_class: source-reported, machiavelli-claim, modern-scholarship, analysis-inference, hypothetical.

nodes.label: Transformation Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: For each aligned information unit: preservation, omission, abstraction, reinterpretation, addition; additions sub-classified other-source | inference | counterfactual | unsupported. Clause-level units make denominators explicit and auditable.

nodes.label: No-Circularity Rule
nodes.rationale: A mechanism derived from Machiavelli may organize questions put to Livy, but Livy's narrative is never counted as independent validation of a mechanism read off Machiavelli; the provenance array makes the derivation path auditable.

nodes.label: Umori (Humors)
nodes.rationale: Machiavelli's general law in Disc. I.7: republics must give legally ordained vents (sfoghi) to the humors (umori) of the collectivity - a one-off psychological explanation in Livy reinterpreted as an institutional design principle.

nodes.label: Otto di Guardia
nodes.rationale: The precise institutional datum 'otto giudici' is chancery knowledge; the claim that eight judges cannot condemn the powerful is an operational observation about tribunal size - one of the few places the implicit data model visibly runs on Florentine administrative detail.

nodes.label: ds:unrest-event-series (B)
nodes.rationale: Trigger domain x resolution channel event series; the variable coding comes from Machiavelli's own ordinario/straordinario distinction - circularity flagged in the dataset record.

nodes.label: ds:war-mobilization-ledger (C)
nodes.rationale: Documented as a negative result: Livy II.35 stages exactly the manpower/morale assessment a chancery secretary wrote for a living, and Machiavelli drops it entirely.

nodes.label: Roman Dictatorship
nodes.rationale: Livy grounds the dictatorship in a legal constraint (magistrates bound by provocatio); Machiavelli grounds it in an epistemic one (a people blinded by a species of false good cannot judge). Same institution, different theory of why republics need it.

nodes.label: Public vs Private Reputation
nodes.rationale: The chapter's theoretical core, with no Livian basis: reputation through private favors (lending money, dowering daughters, defending men from the magistrates) hides a principle of tyranny - 'sotto una opera pia si nasconde uno principio di tirannide'. Each favor type corresponds to a documented Florentine record-producing instrument.

nodes.label: ds:grain-stock-census (B)
nodes.rationale: The Minucian declarations: declarant, stock, monthly-need threshold, forced sale. Structure is Livy's own; values lost; fifth-century historicity doubted (possible retrojection of late-republican annona practice).

nodes.label: ds:distribution-recipient-rolls (C)
nodes.rationale: Who received Maelian grain; needed to test largesse-to-partisans; could not have existed in 440 BCE, did exist in Renaissance Florence (Abbondanza records).

nodes.label: ds:magistrate-fasti (A)
nodes.rationale: The libri lintei citation inside the Maelius episode is the pilot's only directly attested ancient dataset (level A).

nodes.label: Spurius Cassius
nodes.rationale: Omitted wholesale by Machiavelli: the plebs themselves rejected Cassius's largesse as payment for kingship (mercedem regni) and acquiesced in his execution - the datum most awkward for Disc. I.37's clean nobles-vs-plebs frame.

nodes.label: Agrarian Law (Legge Agraria)
nodes.rationale: Machiavelli fuses a 350-year series of distinct measures (Cassius 486, tribunician bills, Licinian cap 367, Gracchan laws 133-121) into one longitudinal 'law' with two fixed clauses - constructing a longitudinal variable out of discrete statutes, an act of data modeling. His 'tanti iugeri' leaves the value field blank: a variable retained, its measurement discarded.

nodes.label: Roba vs Onori
nodes.rationale: Machiavelli's claim (Disc. I.37) that men value property over honors: the nobility yielded honors without extraordinary scandal but defended property until the plebs resorted to extraordinary means; predicts higher conflict intensity for property disputes than honor-access disputes.

nodes.label: Distance-Decay Claim
nodes.rationale: Machiavelli replaces Livy's mechanism for low Antium enrollment (fastidium copia, satiety from abundance) with his own distance-preference reading - the cleanest mechanism-swap in the pilot; testable in principle against enrollment rate x colony distance.

nodes.label: Antium Colony Enrollment (467 BCE)
nodes.rationale: The pilot's unique case of Machiavelli explicitly citing an administrative record as evidence: he calls Livy's remark that few gave their names a 'termine notabile'.

nodes.label: ds:land-tenure-register (C)
nodes.rationale: Enforcement of any iugera cap presupposes a possessor-by-area register; none attested until the Gracchan commission's termini. Machiavelli's implicit data model exceeds the period's attested administrative capacity.

nodes.label: Livy I-X Event Series (383 Events)
nodes.rationale: The first deliverable that does not pass through Machiavelli's selection: 383 events coded by 10 parallel per-book LLM coders blind to the hypotheses, all quotes machine-validated verbatim; the anti-selection-bias denominator.

nodes.label: Legal-Rights Conflict Domain
nodes.rationale: The actually violent domain in Livy I-X (35.3% extraordinary resolution vs ~8% for both property and honors): decemviral tyranny, Verginia, debt-bondage rescues, provocatio crises. Machiavelli has no dedicated variable for it; his roba/onori dichotomy partitions away the category where Livy's violence actually lives - a genuine gap in the recovered ontology, found only by building the denominator.

nodes.label: Selection Bias Quantification (T3)
nodes.rationale: Events in Machiavelli-candidate chapters run 16.2% extraordinary vs 12.5% in unimplicated chapters: he samples toward the violent and dramatic; 74 routine institutional creations in uncited chapters are the dark matter of his exemplum-driven method.

nodes.label: Accusation-Channels Claim (Disc. I.7)
nodes.rationale: Rome's accusation institutions absorbed elite-directed anger: 41 prominent-citizen trials, 82.9% resolved through ordinary channels, trial-to-killing ratio ~2.7:1. Descriptively consistent but untested in the strict sense - the strong test needs within-Rome variation in channel availability, which barely exists in Livy I-X.

nodes.label: 25-Variable Machiavellian Ontology
nodes.rationale: Variables are overwhelmingly institutional and distributional; individual character enters only as reputation-seeking strategy; resource variables appear exclusively as political instruments, never as quantities.

nodes.label: Pressure-and-Channel Model
nodes.rationale: The pilot's central structural finding: Machiavelli's explanatory engine is a pressure-and-channel model, not an actor-psychology model - a political control-system in which flows matter because they open or close channels, not because of their magnitudes.

nodes.label: Ordinary vs Extraordinary Modes (Ordinario/Straordinario)
nodes.rationale: Machiavelli's own mode classifier for conflict resolution; reused as the resolution-channel coding variable of the event series (circularity flagged) and mapped onto authorization regularity in the Persepolis sketch.

nodes.label: Causal-Claim Graph (25 Nodes, 49 Edges)
nodes.rationale: Every edge marked 'historically situated claim, not established causal fact', per the claims-not-facts rule.

nodes.label: Persepolis Fortification Archive (Phase VIII Sketch)
nodes.rationale: Bounded hypothesis generation only: the PFA records allocator, recipient category, commodity, quantity - precisely the distribution-recipient-rolls structure Rome lacks. Parallels are functional analogies, not historical ones; only the distribution-discretion-stability triad transfers to a palace economy.

nodes.label: ds:patronage-network-roster (C)
nodes.rationale: Roman clientela was customary and unregistered; Florentine analogues (ricordanze, Monte delle doti) DID produce records.

nodes.label: Chancery-Experience Hypothesis (Working-Hypothesis Category 2)
nodes.rationale: Chancery experience shaped the variables of Machiavelli's model (category 2 supported), while nothing in the pilot shows he consulted unpublished administrative collections (category 3 unestablished); administrative experience did not make him retain administrative detail.
